name: sil
description: Turn your OpenClaw into an expert shopping agent.

sil_web_url.description: Override for the sil-web origin (the auth authority — token refresh, registration). Falls back to the SIL_WEB_URL env var, then https://sil.4gpts.com.

sil_api_url.description: Override for the sil-api origin (the domain service — sil_whoami's identity read). Distinct from sil_web_url (sil-web). Falls back to the SIL_API_URL env var, then https://sil-api.4gpts.com. Set this at deploy to pin the sil-api host (or to the same origin as sil_web_url if a single gateway fronts both).

sil_web_url.label: sil-web URL (auth)
sil_web_url.help: The sil-web origin — handles registration and token refresh. Override only for staging or self-hosted deployments.

sil_api_url.label: sil-api URL (identity)
sil_api_url.help: The sil-api origin — sil_whoami reads the user's identity here. Distinct from the sil-web URL. Override for staging or self-hosted deployments.

security.packagingNote: Compiled JavaScript ships under ./dist. register() stays synchronous and opens nothing that must be closed: it registers the tools, ensures the data directory, and reads the fourteen JSON Schema artifacts under ./schema so each shopping_* tool can publish its request artifact as its own parameters (seven synchronous readFileSync calls of tracked files inside the package, no network, no timer, no handle). ALL network I/O happens inside a tool's execute(): sil_register calls sil-web over the network, writes tokens.json + config.json to the plugin data directory (owner-only, 0600), and arms a bounded background poll timer that stops on the first terminal claim outcome or after the session deadline. sil_whoami reads the stored session token and calls sil-api for the user's identity, refreshing transparently via sil-web on a 401 (at most one refresh + one retry per call, no timer); a confirmed-dead session clears tokens.json. The seven shopping_* tools read the stored session token and call sil-api's catalog endpoints with it — read-only except shopping_domain_create, which writes one registry row; no timer, but with the SAME bounded 401 recovery as sil_whoami: on a 401 they refresh ONCE via sil-web (rotating tokens.json) and retry the read ONCE; a second 401 or a dead (invalid_grant) refresh token clears tokens.json and is reported as a terminal re-register hint. A non-401 error writes no token. The four document verbs make NO network call and read no token; they read and write the one sil shopper's SINGLETON documents under a fixed $SIL_DATA_DIR/shopper/ (owner-only, files 0600, dirs 0700) as frontmatter-as-truth markdown — there is no manifest and no index file; each file's own frontmatter IS the source of truth, discovered by a filesystem scan. The store is FLAT: shopper/user_spec.md (the person) and shopper/briefs/<slug>.md (one shopping job each), addressed by one ref scheme ("shopper" or "brief:<slug>"). shopping_doc_find scans that frontmatter and returns coordinates only (no bodies) — a document with malformed frontmatter is surfaced as unreadable, never silently dropped or half-read. shopping_doc_read returns ONE whole body plus its frontmatter, answering not_found for an absent document and unreadable for a present-but-corrupt one, which it never writes over. shopping_doc_write takes the WHOLE reconciled markdown body from the caller — there is no append and no in-place section edit, so every change rewrites the whole document — with mode:create fail-closed if the ref already exists and mode:replace fail-closed if it does not. shopping_doc_remove deletes ONE Brief file and never cascades; the shopper document itself is not removable. On first touch of the document surface, the store performs a one-shot migration off the pre-0.5 layout (shopper/domains/<slug>/{method.md, prds/*.md}) into the flat one, deleting a legacy source file only after its replacement reads back, and never deleting bytes under a legacy assets/ directory. sil_doctor is a report-first diagnostic over the SAME $SIL_DATA_DIR state: it reads the data dir, file modes, tokens.json/config.json metadata, and artefact frontmatter, and returns a machine-readable findings array. It reads no token contents out and rotates no token: token health is metadata only (present / mode / parses / expired), where expiry is decoded from the access token's own JWT exp claim strictly LOCALLY (decode-only, no signature verification, no network, no claim other than exp extracted, never a token byte emitted or logged). Its only writes are two safe idempotent fixes under $SIL_DATA_DIR — tightening a too-open mode and creating the missing data dir; a tighten only ever NARROWS (it detects bits set outside the expected mask and chmods to mode & expected, which can only clear bits, never grant them). Enumerated entries under the data dir are lstat'd, and a symlink found among them is REPORTED, never chmod'd-through — that is what keeps a tighten inside the store. The data directory ROOT itself is stat'd rather than lstat'd, because chmod follows a symlink regardless (Linux exposes no lchmod), so lstat there would prevent nothing and merely re-report the same fix forever; a symlinked $SIL_DATA_DIR is an operator-declared indirection, so the tighten lands on the directory the plugin already stores everything in. anything that would mutate the bytes of an existing artefact (clearing a corrupt tokens.json, deleting an orphaned tmp file, repairing a document) is REPORTED as needs_confirmation and never run. It makes exactly ONE outbound request, and it is the only reason https://clawhub.ai is declared: an unauthenticated read-only GET of the published version of @4gpts/sil, bounded by an explicit timeout + abort, carrying no token, no PII, no store contents, and no Authorization header, pinned to that one host (redirects are refused). It fails soft to silence — an unreachable, slow, non-200, or unparseable response yields no finding at all and never fails the run. sil_doctor never acts on the version it reports: it installs nothing, spawns no process, writes no host config, and prompts nobody. The only caller-supplied path segment is a Brief slug, validated (lower-kebab, not "main") before any join; the shopper segment is a compile-time constant. Every write is atomic (tmp file → rename over target → chmod), so a reader sees a whole file or none. The persona is the shopper's host workspace SOUL.md, written by the host CLI (not this plugin, not a sil artefact), and the shopper's host-config wiring is driven separately by the host CLI. The PKCE verifier is held only in memory and is never written to disk. The plugin registers ONE gateway RPC method, sil.search_results (scope operator.read, which the host authorizes before the handler runs): a paired client calls it over the already-authenticated deviceToken WS to read back a shopping_search page whose callId it already saw on the tool frames. It opens no socket, no port, and no route — registering it hands the host a closure, and the host owns the transport. The pages it serves live in a bounded IN-MEMORY buffer that is never written to disk: shopping_search stores its own successful result there under the callId the host passed it (at most 32 pages, dropped 15 minutes after the search, evicted lazily on the next write with no timer, and gone entirely when the process exits). The method makes no network call, starts no agent run, and returns a page only to the sil account that produced it — every unknown, expired, or foreign reference gets one identical not-found body. Artefact bodies, tokens, and identity PII are never logged; the method logs only whether a page was found and how many products it held.
filesystemScope: $SIL_DATA_DIR (default $XDG_DATA_HOME/sil, else ~/.local/share/sil) — tokens.json, config.json, shopper/user_spec.md + shopper/briefs/<slug>.md (the ONE sil shopper's singleton documents: the person, and one document per shopping job. Frontmatter-as-truth with no manifest and no index file; shopping_doc_write writes a whole reconciled body, shopping_doc_remove removes one Brief. The `shopper` and `briefs` segments are fixed compile-time constants, not caller input; a Brief slug is the only caller-supplied path segment, validated (lower-kebab, not "main") before any join. A pre-0.5 store is migrated in place on first touch, which reads and deletes shopper/domains/<slug>/{method.md, prds/*.md} but never any bytes under a legacy assets/ directory. All writes are atomic + owner-only (files 0600, dirs 0700). The persona is the host workspace SOUL.md, not a sil document)
